subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Caffeine and Anxiety
description: A quick, practical guide to Caffeine and Anxiety.

hook.text: Caffeine and anxiety share the same symptoms: racing heart, restlessness, and difficulty concentrating.

buildup.text: Caffeine stimulates the sympathetic nervous system—the body's fight-or-flight response—increasing adrenaline release.

discovery.text: In people with anxiety disorders, even moderate doses (200 mg) can trigger panic attacks indistinguishable from the real thing.

twist.text: Many people treat anxiety with medication while consuming 400+ mg of caffeine daily—unknowingly working against treatment.

climax.text: Cutting caffeine is one of the first recommendations psychiatrists make for patients with anxiety disorders.

punchline.text: For some brains, caffeine isn't alertness—it's anxiety in a cup.

quiz.question: Why can caffeine trigger panic attacks in some people?
options: It stimulates the fight-or-flight response, mimicking anxiety symptoms

details.summary: At high doses caffeine can trigger or worsen anxiety by stimulating the sympathetic nervous system and increasing cortisol and adrenaline. People with anxiety disorders are especially sensitive, and some experience panic-like symptoms from as little as 200 milligrams.
details.whyItMatters: The link between caffeine and anxiety is often overlooked. Reducing intake can be a simple, effective first step for managing anxiety symptoms.
takeaways: High caffeine doses activate the fight-or-flight response
People with anxiety disorders are more sensitive to caffeine
Cutting caffeine is often recommended as an anxiety intervention

faq.question: How much caffeine typically triggers anxiety symptoms in sensitive people?
faq.answer: Sensitive individuals may notice anxiety from as little as 100 to 200 milligrams, roughly one cup of coffee. Those with diagnosed anxiety disorders are often advised to stay below 100 milligrams daily or eliminate caffeine entirely.

faq.question: Can switching from coffee to tea reduce caffeine-related anxiety?
faq.answer: Yes. Tea contains less caffeine per cup and also provides L-theanine, which promotes calm alertness. Many people who experience coffee-related anxiety find tea provides gentler stimulation without the jitters.
